docs.text: cert-manager-webhook-nameshield A cert-manager ACME DNS01 solver webhook for the Nameshield DNS API . It lets cert-manager complete Let's Encrypt (or any ACME) dns-01 challenges by creating and deleting _acme-challenge TXT records in zones managed by Nameshield. Based on cert-manager/webhook-example . How it works For each challenge, cert-manager sends a ChallengeRequest to the webhook, which: Resolves the Nameshield API token: from the Kubernetes Secret referenced by apiTokenSecretRef , or from the NAMESHIELD_TOKEN environment variable when ambient credentials are allowed (test suite). Determines the Nameshield zone: explicit zoneName from the solver configuration if set; otherwise the zone resolved by cert-manager ( resolvedZone ), when it exists in the account; otherwise discovery by probing parent names, most specific first. Present : creates the TXT record (idempotent), then calls the zone validation endpoint, because the Nameshield API keeps changes pending until validated. CleanUp : finds the TXT record by name and value, deletes it, then validates the zone again. Nameshield API specifics handled by the webhook Authentication: Authorization: Bearer <token> . TXT record data must be wrapped in double quotes. Changes are only applied after POST /zones/{zone}/validate . Rate limit of 600 requests per 5 minutes per token, with Retry-After handling and retry on 429/5xx. Record deletion requires the record ID, obtained by listing records. Published artifacts Container image on GitHub Container Registry: ghcr.io/dotinfra/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield . Helm chart repository on GitHub Pages, served from the root of this same site: https://dotinfra.github.io/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield ( index.yaml ). docs.text: Configuration Two levels of configuration exist: the solver configuration , set per-Issuer in the webhook.config stanza; the Helm chart values , set at install/upgrade time. Solver configuration The webhook solver configuration, set in the Issuer's webhook.config stanza: Field Type Description apiUrl string Nameshield DNS API base URL. Default: https://api.nameshield.net/dns/v4 . Use https://ote-api.nameshield.net/dns/v4 for the OTE environment. apiTokenSecretRef object Required. name and key of the Secret holding the API token. Optional namespace ; defaults to the challenge namespace (the cert-manager namespace for ClusterIssuers). zoneName string Optional. Forces the Nameshield zone to update, bypassing zone resolution and discovery. ttl int Optional. TTL of created TXT records. Provider default when unset. includeOtherUsersChanges bool Optional, default false. Set to true to also apply pending zone changes made by other users when validating. Helm chart values Defaults are in deploy/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield/values.yaml : Value Default Description groupName cert-manager-webhook-nameshield Kubernetes APIService group of the webhook. Referenced by the chart's APIService and by each Issuer's groupName field. Must be unique in the cluster and stable once deployed. certManager.namespace cert-manager Namespace of the cert-manager controller. certManager.serviceAccountName cert-manager ServiceAccount of the cert-manager controller. image.repository ghcr.io/dotinfra/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield Webhook container image repository. image.tag "" (falls back to .Chart.AppVersion ) Webhook container image tag. A released chart points at the Docker tag of the same release. image.pullPolicy IfNotPresent Image pull policy. nameOverride / fullnameOverride "" Standard Helm name overrides. replicaCount 1 Number of webhook replicas. service.type / service.port ClusterIP / 443 Webhook Service type and port. rbac.allowClusterWideSecretAccess false Install a ClusterRole granting the webhook read access to Secrets cluster-wide, for Issuers in other namespaces without an explicit apiTokenSecretRef.namespace . resources {} Container resource requests/limits. nodeSelector / tolerations / affinity {} Standard pod scheduling knobs. Limitations A single API token is used for all zones managed by the webhook. Zone discovery probes successive parent names; with many unrelated zones per token, set zoneName explicitly in each solver config. The ns records at the zone apex are never touched by this webhook; all changes concern _acme-challenge TXT records and the zone validation endpoint.

docs.text: Development Build and test Build the webhook image from source: make build-image IMAGE=ghcr.io/dotinfra/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield TAG=0.1.0 make push-image IMAGE=ghcr.io/dotinfra/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield TAG=0.1.0 Unit tests (no external dependency): make unit-test The cert-manager DNS01 conformance suite requires a real Nameshield zone and API token, plus the envtest binaries (downloaded automatically): export NAMESHIELD_ZONE=example.com # a zone hosted by Nameshield export NAMESHIELD_TOKEN=<api-token> # token with DNS rights on that zone make test All DNS webhooks deployed publicly are expected to run and pass this suite. Render the chart locally: make rendered-manifest IMAGE=ghcr.io/dotinfra/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield TAG=0.1.0 Documentation This site is built with MkDocs from the docs/ folder ( mkdocs.yml at the repository root). To preview it locally: pip install mkdocs==1.6.1 mkdocs serve The docs.yaml workflow builds the site on every push/PR touching docs/ , mkdocs.yml or the workflow, and publishes it on main to the root of the gh-pages branch, so the documentation is the GitHub Pages home page. The Helm chart repository ( index.yaml ) is preserved at the same root. CI and releases Three GitHub Actions workflows are defined in .github/workflows/ : ci.yaml — runs on every push and pull request on main : gofmt check, go vet ./... , unit tests ( go test ./nameshield/... ), helm lint and helm template on deploy/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield , and a Docker image build (load only, no push). docs.yaml — builds the MkDocs site and publishes it to the root of gh-pages , as the Pages home page (see above). release.yaml — runs on push of a v* tag only (one tag = one release, no extra chart tags/releases): validates the semver tag, builds and pushes the multi-arch image to GHCR ( <version> , <major>.<minor> , <major> , latest on stable releases, sha-<short-sha> ), sets the chart version / appVersion to the tag version, packages it with helm package , creates the single GitHub release on the tag with the .tgz attached, and publishes the .tgz + regenerated index.yaml to the gh-pages branch (chart repository at the root of the Pages site, next to the documentation). All workflows rely on the default GITHUB_TOKEN only — no extra secrets are required. Cutting a release git tag vX.Y.Z git push origin vX.Y.Z Everything is aligned on the same release version: the Docker tag X.Y.Z , the chart version / appVersion X.Y.Z , and the chart's default image.tag (which equals appVersion , i.e. X.Y.Z ). GitHub Pages setup In Settings → Pages , set Build and deployment to Deploy from a branch and select the gh-pages branch with the / (root) folder. The site then serves, from the same branch: the documentation at the root, https://dotinfra.github.io/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield/ (home page); the Helm chart repository at https://dotinfra.github.io/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield/index.yaml ( .tgz archives at the root). The gh-pages branch itself is created automatically (as an empty orphan branch) by the release workflow on the first chart publication. Project layout .github/workflows/ CI, docs and release workflows main.go Entrypoint, registers the solver nameshield/solver.go webhook.Solver: Present / CleanUp / Initialize nameshield/client.go Nameshield DNS API v4 client (records, validation) nameshield/config.go Solver configuration schema nameshield/solver_test.go Unit tests main_test.go cert-manager DNS01 conformance suite testdata/nameshield/ Conformance suite solver configuration docs/ MkDocs documentation sources mkdocs.yml MkDocs site configuration deploy/... Helm chart Dockerfile Multi-stage build

docs.text: Installation Pre-built artifacts are published automatically by the CI (see Development ): container image on GitHub Container Registry: ghcr.io/dotinfra/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield (tags <version> , <major>.<minor> , <major> , latest on stable releases, and sha-<short-sha> ); Helm chart repository on GitHub Pages: https://dotinfra.github.io/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield . 1. Install the Helm chart helm repo add cert-manager-webhook-nameshield https://dotinfra.github.io/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield helm repo update helm install cert-manager-webhook-nameshield cert-manager-webhook-nameshield/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield \ --namespace cert-manager \ --create-namespace \ --set groupName=cert-manager-webhook-nameshield The chart defaults to the published image ghcr.io/dotinfra/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield:<appVersion> : the chart's image.tag defaults to .Chart.AppVersion , so a released chart always points at the Docker tag published for the same release. Override it with --set image.tag=<tag> . To install from a local checkout with a self-built image instead: helm install cert-manager-webhook-nameshield deploy/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield \ --namespace cert-manager \ --set groupName=cert-manager-webhook-nameshield \ --set image.repository=<your-registry>/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield \ --set image.tag=<tag> 2. Create the API token Secret The token must have DNS rights on the zones involved. For ClusterIssuers, the Secret must exist in the cert-manager cluster resource namespace (default cert-manager ): kubectl -n cert-manager create secret generic nameshield-api-token \ --from-literal=token=<NAMESHIELD_TOKEN> The groupName value names the Kubernetes APIService group of the webhook. It must be unique in the cluster and stable once deployed. By default the chart installs a Role granting the webhook read access to Secrets in its own namespace only. If Issuers live in other namespaces and apiTokenSecretRef does not specify a namespace, set rbac.allowClusterWideSecretAccess=true . 3. Reference the solver in an Issuer Create a ClusterIssuer (or Issuer ) whose dns01 stanza uses the webhook solver with the groupName configured above and the solver name nameshield : apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1 kind: ClusterIssuer metadata: name: letsencrypt-nameshield spec: acme: server: https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory email: admin@example.com privateKeySecretRef: name: letsencrypt-account-key solvers: - dns01: webhook: groupName: cert-manager-webhook-nameshield solverName: nameshield config: apiTokenSecretRef: name: nameshield-api-token key: token # namespace: cert-manager # rarely needed, see below # zoneName: example.com # optional: force the Nameshield zone # apiUrl: https://ote-api.nameshield.net/dns/v4 # OTE environment # ttl: 60 # optional TXT record TTL The config stanza accepts the fields documented in Configuration . For a ClusterIssuer , cert-manager resolves apiTokenSecretRef in its own cluster resource namespace ( cert-manager by default), so namespace can usually be omitted and the Secret created in step 2 is found as-is. Set namespace explicitly when it differs, or set rbac.allowClusterWideSecretAccess=true on the chart. Then request a certificate: apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1 kind: Certificate metadata: name: example-com namespace: default spec: secretName: example-com-tls dnsNames: - example.com - www.example.com issuerRef: name: letsencrypt-nameshield kind: ClusterIssuer Building the image from source make build-image IMAGE=ghcr.io/dotinfra/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield TAG=0.1.0 make push-image IMAGE=ghcr.io/dotinfra/cert-manager-webhook-nameshield TAG=0.1.0 then install the chart from the local checkout as shown above.
